# Performance verdict: PR 312, round 1

**PASS WITH NOTES** at `6f4c3b9010109bf5532864e48dcaa59d97603050`.
No performance block. Deployed AFTER is owed; this is not a claim that the
daemon has already become cheaper.

## Cost and scope

The PR adds no loop, poll, timer, cache or process-launch site. It changes
the in-process SQL used by each pane-filtered registry list, including whoami
and adopt. Copilot status lines retain their existing 10-second refresh:
request rate scales with sessions, plus Claude hooks and explicit callers.
The packet's roughly 8-10 calls/s is a historical baseline, not a cap.

Before: a full historical-seat walk in id-index order. After: a pane-index
seek, matching-row reads, and a temporary B-tree for `ORDER BY id`.
`EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN` explicitly reports that remaining sort. With N seats
and K matches, the lookup is bounded by the seek and K rather than a full
N-row scan; sorting can still cost O(K log K). Storage is O(N), and inserts
and updates that assign pane maintain one additional index. Mechanical
state-only updates do not add pane-index maintenance.

This is non-destructive: it introduces no deletion policy or safety brake.
The intentional missing-index refusal is a cost invariant, not a retention
or authorization policy.

## Independent SQL receipt

Command: `nice -n 19 python3 pr312_probe.py sql <receipt.json>`, from the
exact-head review checkout. The session-local probe reads the two SQL
constants directly from `crates/store/src/registry.rs`, opens the live
source with `mode=ro` and `query_only`, copies only the seats table and its
existing indexes in one read transaction, and closes the source before
any writes. Every migration, insert, update and drop below ran on the
disposable copy. That copy was deleted on completion.

November 21, 2026, 06:31:49 UTC; SQLite 3.54.1; 3,252 seat rows;
1,738 distinct non-null panes; busiest pane 112 rows. Seven batches of
200 cached executions after 20 warmups, fetching every result column:

| Lookup | CPU ms before -> after | Wall ms before -> after |
|---|---|---|
| Busiest, 112 rows | 0.730 -> 0.224 | 0.732 -> 0.227 |
| One row | 0.528 -> 0.00868 | 0.531 -> 0.00869 |
| Absent pane | 0.517 -> 0.00557 | 0.519 -> 0.00558 |

All three new plans say `SEARCH seats USING INDEX seats_by_pane (pane=?)`,
then `USE TEMP B-TREE FOR ORDER BY`; the generic plan says
`SCAN seats USING INDEX sqlite_autoindex_seats_1`.
The direction and reduced visited work are reproduced. These timings
include Python tuple materialization and are not a reproduction of the
author's sqlite3 CLI ratios, cold-cache behavior or SQLx route latency.

Migration 0048 added 45,056 bytes (44 KiB) to this seats-only database.
One measured run took 7.698 ms wall / 1.828 ms CPU; integrity_check was ok.
This measures the index build on the existing seat population, not a copy
of the entire 2.48 GB store or its boot sequence.

Write probe: median of seven 1,000-row rolled-back batches, no durable
commit/fsync latency. CPU microseconds per statement:

| Statement | Before | After | Extra |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Insert | 3.294 | 3.729 | 0.435 |
| Change pane | 1.271 | 1.822 | 0.551 |
| Assign the same pane | 1.235 | 1.695 | 0.460 |
| State-only update | 1.295 | 1.274 | No measurable increase |

These are index-maintenance microprobes, not end-to-end event-sourced
registry transaction timings. Their absolute overhead is small.

216 combinations of harness, folder, parent, pane and live-only filters
returned identical full rows in identical order between the two queries.
Dropping the index on the copy made the new SQL refuse with
`no such index: seats_by_pane`, as intended.

## Live BEFORE receipt

Command: `nice -n 19 python3 pr312_probe.py live <receipt.json>`;
two `pij-rs --json ping` reads and single-PID `/bin/ps` samples.
November 21, 2026, 06:31:59.581 -> 06:32:59.615 UTC:

- Same PID 31125, deployed commit `fb565c165d`, process start
  November 21, 2026, 16:06:56 local time; interval 60.033353 s.
- Whoami ok count 14,944 -> 15,614: 670 completions, zero refusals,
  11.1605 calls/s. active_us 28,847,447 -> 30,258,359:
  1,410,912 us, **2.10584 ms active wall time/completion**; held_us stayed 0.
- Daemon cumulative CPU 288.32 -> 299.83 seconds:
  **19.173% of one core**, not whoami's exclusive CPU.
  RSS 140,304 -> 130,992 KiB.
- One-minute host load 97.551 -> 111.161. Registry cohorts stayed
  84 Copilot, 106 Claude and 6 OMP untombstoned rows; those counts are
  not a process-liveness census or exact status-line consumer counts.
- Exact daemon launches 989 -> 998: 9 in total, 0.1499/s.
  Only `ddocs.community` +2 and `git.community` +7 changed.
  Every tmux and process-probe site was flat; site deltas reconcile to total.

Separate subsequent `harness/scripts/nice19.sh just spawn-rate --seconds 20 --json`:
20.0 seconds, PID 31125, **269.3 machine launches/s**, sampled 250.9/s;
attributed daemon children 0.4/s lower bound. Attribution is sampled,
not exact; the statusline script-marker count misses exec'd native
statusline processes. This busy sampler did not overlap the CPU window.
These are BEFORE readings only and do not establish a feature-specific
whole-machine launch reduction.

## Proof and remaining notes

`just pr-freeze 312`: FINAL at the exact full SHA, main base, CLEAN,
latest CI 5/5, migration 48 above main's 47. `git diff --check` passed;
the detached checkout stayed clean. Relative to the merge's main parent,
only the five B1 files differ; both D-F258-1 and D-F258-2 are present.

Exact-head CI run 44875077557, attempt 1, succeeded. Its successful
rust-test job 136757885002 uploaded artifact **14695023977**; that
artifact's head_sha is the full reviewed SHA. JUnit contains 2,754 cases,
zero failures/errors, including both registry_pane_index tests and the
forward/reopen migration tests. No local cargo build or test was started.
`harness boot` was attempted: advisory NOT-READY because this C25
read-only checkout has no node_modules. Local TS and the full
`harness checks` were not run or represented as green; TS proof is the
exact-head CI, and full local gate evidence remains the author's PR receipt.

Optional test improvement, not a block (C34): the cost test explains the
exported SQL constant, not the statement actually selected by
`SqliteRegistry::list`. Removing the runtime branch would leave its
plan assertion intact. An executed-query cost tripwire would close that
future-regression gap; the current branch is visibly wired correctly.

**Owed after the prime's deploy:** repeat the same PID/start/commit-bound
60-second whoami active/held, launch-site, CPU/RSS, host-load and cohort
window, plus the separate 20-second machine launch sampler. Do not
infer deployed CPU savings from this SQL-only result.

**magicWand:** one read-only cost-window command that captures route
active/held deltas, PID/start/build, CPU/RSS, load and registry cohorts
together, with a separate machine sampler.

**difficulties:** C25 makes local TS/full-gate proof unavailable here;
the author and independent SQL probes use different engines/materialization
paths, so their absolute timings must retain their protocols.
Performance/312 remains held until merge.
